[ASSISTANT_SAID] Stanford University offers a Master of Science in Data Science (MS-DS) with a curriculum covering machine learning, statistics, data visualization, and data engineering.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The duration of the Stanford MS-DS program is designed to be completed in 2-3 years, with classes held on weeknights and occasional weekends.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Admission requirements for Stanford MS-DS include a Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field, a recommended GPA of 3.5 or higher, and prerequisite courses in Linear Algebra, Calculus, Probability, and Programming (Python or R).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) offers a Master of Business Analytics (MBAn) focusing on applying data science to business problems.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The duration of the MIT MBAn program is designed to be completed in 18-24 months, with classes held on weeknights and occasional weekends.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Admission requirements for MIT MBAn include a Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field, a recommended GPA of 3.5 or higher, and prerequisite courses in Calculus, Probability, and Statistics.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] University of California, Berkeley offers a Master of Science in Data Science (MS-DS) with a curriculum covering machine learning, data engineering, and data visualization.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The duration of the UC Berkeley MS-DS program is designed to be completed in 2-3 years, with classes held on weeknights and occasional weekends.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Admission requirements for UC Berkeley MS-DS include a Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field, a recommended GPA of 3.0 or higher, and prerequisite courses in Linear Algebra, Calculus, Probability, and Programming (Python or R).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] GRE scores are recommended for Stanford MS-DS but not required; for MIT MBAn, GRE scores are required; for UC Berkeley MS-DS, GRE scores are required.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For Stanford MS-DS, if GRE scores are submitted, focus on the Quantitative Reasoning section.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For MIT MBAn, the middle 80% of admitted students typically score 164-170 in Quantitative Reasoning.
